title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page. Over Q there is an algebraic envelope Π_Q ⊂ 𝔊_Q ⊂ M_Q of a discrete situation Π_0 ⊂ 𝔊_0 → M. Π_0 is a discrete group with 'loops'. M is an arithmetic, Teichmüller/Galois-type group acting on it. χ_M : M_Q → G_m,Q is presumably the cyclotomic-type character. Grothendieck chooses a Z-model M of M_Q and takes the schematic closures Π, 𝔊 of Π_Q, 𝔊_Q in it. This gives group schemes over Z with quotients T, Γ, N (representability via Raynaud), factorizations (47) through Π(Z), 𝔊(Z), M(Ẑ), and the extension of χ_M to M → G_m,Z, which factors through Γ.

This page does two things.

(i) It poses a problem. Find an existence theorem, perhaps even a uniqueness theorem under stronger hypotheses, for a SMOOTH model M over Z of M_Q such that:
- the discrete group M maps into M(Z);
- χ_M extends to a homomorphism M → G_m,Z.

(ii) It addresses a difficulty. Over Q the 'exterior homomorphisms' (43), k_i : T_i → Π (one per loop/cusp i), exist. Over Z they will not in general extend as they stand to homomorphisms T_i,Z → Π.

The workaround is as follows.
1. Take the centralizer L̃_{i,0} = Centr_{Π_0}(k_i : T_0 → Π_0). Here T_0 is a lattice; for a single loop T_0 ≅ Z.
2. This centralizer is an arithmetic group, virtually T_0, related to Aut(T_0 → Π_0) by a normal subgroup of finite index.
3. The map (50), L̃_{i,0} → Π(Z), is 'continuously unipotent'. By the universal property of the envelope over Z (§50, 4°, p. 658'ff), it factors through a homomorphism of Z-group schemes (51), Env(L̃_{i,0}) → Π.
4. On the next page this factors further through one of the smooth quotients Z_{i,n} of Env (the next page's 'End' is a slip for Env). These are extensions (52): 1 → (nT_0)_vector-group → Z_{i,n} → constant finite group L̃_{i,0}/nT_0 → 1 over Spec Z.

The key observation on the next page: the restriction of Z_{i,n} → Π to the identity component (the additive group attached to nT_0) is in general not a monomorphism. If it is one for n, it fails for proper multiples n'. The favourable case is when some n gives a mono (53). This amounts to saying that the schematic closure in Π of the one-parameter additive subgroup k_i(G_a,Q) is a smooth subgroup scheme.

Why this can fail is the standard phenomenon. The closure of t ↦ exp(tN) in a unipotent Z-group has coordinate ring generated by the divided-power/binomial functions binom(t,k). That ring is not Z[t], so the closure is a non-smooth model of G_a.

Purpose: to build integral (over Z) models of the algebraic envelopes of the anabelian/Teichmüller data in the Longue Marche, so that the inertia (cusp) subgroups and the cyclotomic character have meaning over Spec Z and not only over Q or over Ẑ.
errors: Phrase about Aut: as written ('Aut(T_0 →k_i Π_0) y est un sous-groupe distingué d'indice fini') the containment direction is ambiguous. The natural correct statement is that the centralizer is normal of finite index in the stabilizer/normalizer of k_i, the quotient embedding in Aut(T_0). Alternatively, Aut(T_0→Π_0) means something like the centralizer modulo the image of T_0. Either reading needs a finiteness hypothesis on the image in Aut(T_0).
Next-page 'End(L̃_{i,0})' must be Env(L̃_{i,0}), the envelope.

The claim that the centralizer is an 'arithmetic group' is asserted without proof. In the virtually-T_0 case it is trivially true, but in general (e.g. mapping-class-type Π_0) it is a nontrivial hypothesis.

The existence/uniqueness of a smooth Z-model M with M → M(Z) and χ_M extending is only posed. Uniqueness certainly fails without further conditions, as Grothendieck himself hedges ('moyennant des conditions plus fortes').

ideas.what: Problem of existence (and uniqueness) of a smooth Z-model of the algebraic envelope M_Q such that the discrete group lands in its Z-points and the character χ extends to G_m,Z
ideas.modern_name: Smooth integral models of algebraic groups / of algebraic hulls of arithmetic groups (cf. Bruhat–Tits / Néron-type models, Prasad–Yu)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bruhat–Tits (local smooth models), Néron; global Z-models of linear groups treated in SGA3 / Raynaud contexts
ideas.where_published: Not in this form; related representability of quotients is Raynaud (Faisceaux amples..., LNM 119)

ideas.what: Universal property: a 'continuously unipotent' homomorphism from a discrete group Γ to G(Z), G a Z-group scheme, factors through a Z-group-scheme envelope Env(Γ)
ideas.modern_name: Integral unipotent / pro-algebraic completion (hull) of a discrete group over Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malcev, Quillen (over Q); Hain (relative/weighted completions, over Q); integral versions scattered (e.g. Bass–Lubotzky, Hain–Matsumoto over Q_l)
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished notes (§50, 4°, p. 658')

ideas.what: Centralizer of an inertia (loop) homomorphism k_i : T_0 → Π_0 as replacement for an extension of k_i over Z
ideas.modern_name: Centralizers of cuspidal/inertia subgroups; decomposition-type subgroups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Anabelian geometry literature (Nakamura, Mochizuki on cuspidal inertia)
ideas.where_published: Spirit of Esquisse / Longue Marche (lacets, multiplicateurs)

ideas.what: Smooth quotients of Env of a virtually-abelian group are extensions of a finite constant group by vector groups attached to sublattices nT_0, but the induced map to Π is generally not a monomorphism, and the favourable case corresponds to the closure of a G_a being smooth
ideas.modern_name: Non-smoothness of schematic closures of one-parameter unipotent subgroups over Z (binomial / divided-power models of G_a)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in integral models of unipotent groups

missed.claim: Existence and, under stronger hypotheses, uniqueness of a smooth Z-model of the algebraic envelope of the Teichmüller/Galois-type group M. The model should receive M in its Z-points and carry an extension of the cyclotomic-type character to G_m,Z. This is posed as a goal and not carried out.
missed.quote: Il serait intéressant de dégager un th. d'existence, (voire même d'unicité, moyennant des conditions plus fortes peut-être) d'un "modèle" M lisse sur Z de M_Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral (Spec Z) versions of motivic/Teichmüller-type completions (Hain–Matsumoto weighted completions are over Q or Q_l) are still largely undeveloped. Grothendieck frames the question as a concrete smooth-model problem with a character condition.

missed.claim: Grothendieck uses an integral envelope Env(Γ) of discrete groups, with a universal property for 'continuously unipotent' maps to Z-points of group schemes, as the tool to put inertia/cusp data of anabelian objects over Spec Z.
missed.quote: qui est cont. unipotent - il se factorise donc par un hom. de schémas en groupes Env(L̃_{i,0}) → Π
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links integral algebraic hulls of discrete groups with anabelian cusp structures over Z. Most later work (Hain, Matsumoto, Deligne's motivic π_1) stays over fields.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished program for Z-integral models of algebraic envelopes in the Longue Marche, built on Grothendieck's own notion of integral envelope. It is interesting as a record, but the concrete statements on the page are either posed problems or standard phenomena (non-smooth closures of G_a over Z).
transcription_corrections: Margin '212' is the archive page number; '754.' is Grothendieck's own pagination.
The struck word before '(T_0 →k_i Π_0)' appears to be 'Aut' (or 'Hom'), crossed out yet effectively still meant as 'Aut(T_0 → Π_0)'.
'(M — M(Z)' likely denotes a map M → M(Z) (compare the previous page's M → M(Ẑ)).
'{+k_i+}' is an insertion clarifying that the exterior homomorphisms (43) are the k_i; the '✓' marks the insertion point.
